impact: Per GTIG: a live dashboard organising, validating and managing more than 23,800 harvested secrets, including API keys for cloud and AI services. Victims and follow-on use are not described.
mitigations: GTIG disabled the assets associated with the activity.
GTIG frames enterprise AI assets, including API credentials and cloud compute quotas, as high-value targets and recommends secure-AI practices and defensive use of AI.
name: GTIG 'Recon': exposed agentic C2 framework managed more than 23,800 harvested secrets

sources.title: GTIG AI Threat Tracker: From Prompting to Autonomy - The Evolution of Adversarial AI
Hackers build AI frameworks for widescale credential theft

summary: In its September 2026 AI Threat Tracker, Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) reported finding an exposed command-and-control server hosting an automated reconnaissance and credential-management framework dubbed "Recon". Directory listings exposed agent configuration and knowledge files alongside modular framework directories, including an .openclaw/ directory and a memory directory. Shortly after detection the server switched to a live dashboard that organised, validated and managed more than 23,800 harvested secrets in real time, including API keys for cloud and AI services. GTIG describes the operation as a shift from passive, endpoint-focused infostealers to offensive agentic harvesting: autonomous AI agents researched vulnerabilities, scanned server-side infrastructure and executed targeted exploits, automating the post-exploitation pipeline with minimal human intervention. GTIG disabled the associated assets. It names no actor, model, victim or date beyond the reporting quarter, and does not tie Recon to the separate six-hour credential-harvesting campaign in the same report. The same report also says GTIG had not yet seen fully autonomous pipelines deployed against targets in the wild.
